name: Cessna 401/402/404 Titan
summary: Unpressurized six-to-ten-seat twin built from 1966 into the 1980s, a mainstay of air-taxi, cargo and small commuter operators.

wings: Early 401/402 carry large tip tanks; the 402C and 404 have plain tips
engines: Two turbocharged flat-six engines in long nacelles
fuselage: Long, straight-sided cabin with a row of oval or rounded-square windows
Long pointed nose with a baggage compartment
Large cargo door on the left rear

tellTales: Long, straight-sided twin with a row of rounded windows and a pointed nose
Large tip tanks on many examples
Tall, squared-off swept fin above a low tail

confusedWith.howToTell: The 310 is smaller and slimmer with a shorter cabin; the 402 has a longer, deeper cabin that seats six to ten.
The 340/414/421 are pressurized with small porthole-like windows on a portly cabin; the 402 is unpressurized with a longer, straighter cabin.
The Navajo has a tapered wing with plain tips and a dorsal strake on the fin; early 402s have wingtip tanks and a more squared-off fin.

usCount.source: FAA Releasable Aircraft Database — valid registrations
